title: Generic types and stability in strongly minimal theories

based_on.title: Model Theory of Groups
based_on.pages: Definition 2.25 and Proposition 2.26, p.8 (revision 2018-05-21); arbitrary parameter-set argument expanded

based_on.title: Lecture Notes on Stability Theory
based_on.pages: Section 2.2, Exercise 2.4, p.11 (revision 2017-08-27); the finite-tuple counting proof is supplied here

summary: Construct the unique generic one-type, count finite-tuple types, and derive omega-stability and countable saturated and prime models.
abstract: In an infinite equality structure, an element either equals a named point or satisfies the one remaining complete description. Strong minimality extends this distinction from equality to every unary formula: each definable set is finite or has finite complement. All cofinite conditions fit together into one complete type, whose realizations are precisely the points outside algebraic closure of the parameters. Every other type is confined to a finite definable set and is already realized in the original model. Counting formulas bounds the algebraic closure and leaves only this one additional generic type. A small-model argument then counts finite tuples by their prefix type and a remaining one-type, extending the same bound to every finite tuple length. In a countable language this proves omega-stability and smallness, and hence the existence of countable saturated and prime models.
